provenance.title: WHO Labour Care Guide — intrapartum parameter monitoring
provenance.why: The Labour Care Guide replaced the classic partograph because the fixed 1 cm/hour alert line labelled many normal labours as obstructed and drove avoidable caesareans. This pack is the LCG monitoring layer: each observed parameter is assessed against its own reference threshold, and the guide's central teaching — that slow cervical progress alone is not an indication for caesarean section — is preserved rather than re-imported through a rate line.

sourceVerification.note: There is no WHO SMART DAK for the Labour Care Guide, so this is authored from the published 2020 guide, not extracted from a pinned artefact — the same ENGINEERING_SEED status as the MEC and SPR packs. The parameter alert thresholds below (fetal heart rate, maternal pulse, temperature, blood pressure, contractions, liquor, moulding) are well-established intrapartum values and are transcribed here; they still require line-by-line ratification against the primary text. blocksRatification stays true.
sourceVerification.deferred: The LCG cervical-dilation REFERENCE THRESHOLD (progress of labour over time) and the 'slow progress alone is not a caesarean indication' decision rule are DELIBERATELY NOT in this pack yet. They are the guide's genuinely novel element — the permissive replacement for the 1 cm/hour line — and encoding an approximate progress curve under a WHO citation would be exactly the fabrication this repository forbids. They land with the freeze-and-demote of PartographProgressEngine, where the classic constants are migrated to governed content and the reinterpretation can be cross-checked against the primary text. This pack asserts the monitoring standard and the parameter alerts; it does not yet decide progress.

rules.name: Fetal heart rate outside the reference range
rules.message: Fetal heart rate outside 110–160 — assess the fetus.
rules.explanation: A baseline fetal heart rate below 110 or above 160 bpm is outside the LCG reference range and needs assessment of fetal wellbeing and its cause — maternal position, hydration, fever, hypotension, cord or placental compromise.
rules.requiredAction: Reposition the mother, check for reversible causes (fever, hypotension, dehydration), listen through and after a contraction, and escalate if it does not recover.
sourceRefs: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) — fetal heart rate

adaptation.whoStatement: The Labour Care Guide flags a fetal heart rate below 110 or above 160 bpm as requiring attention.
evidenceRefs: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) — fetal heart rate

rules.name: Meconium-stained or blood-stained liquor
rules.message: Liquor is meconium- or blood-stained — increase fetal surveillance.
rules.explanation: Meconium — especially thick — and blood-stained liquor are LCG alert findings associated with fetal compromise and abruption respectively, and they change the surveillance and the birth plan.
rules.requiredAction: Increase fetal monitoring, look for a cause, and prepare for the possibility of neonatal resuscitation and a more urgent birth.
sourceRefs: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) — amniotic fluid

adaptation.whoStatement: The Labour Care Guide flags meconium-stained and blood-stained amniotic fluid as findings requiring attention.
evidenceRefs: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) — amniotic fluid

rules.name: Severe fetal skull moulding
rules.message: Severe moulding (+3) — a sign of possible obstruction.
rules.explanation: Moulding of +3 (bones overlapping and not reducible) suggests cephalopelvic disproportion and possible obstructed labour, and it is read together with progress and descent, not alone.
rules.requiredAction: Assess for obstructed labour — descent, progress, the cause — and escalate for a decision about mode of birth. Do not read moulding in isolation.

adaptation.whoStatement: The Labour Care Guide flags moulding of +3 as a finding requiring attention.

rules.name: Tachysystole — too many contractions
rules.message: More than five contractions in ten minutes — reduce uterine activity.
rules.explanation: More than five contractions in ten minutes is tachysystole, which reduces placental perfusion between contractions and threatens the fetus. It is most often oxytocin-driven and reversible.
rules.requiredAction: If oxytocin is running, reduce or stop it; reposition the mother; reassess the fetal heart. Tachysystole with an abnormal fetal heart rate is an emergency.

adaptation.whoStatement: The Labour Care Guide flags more than five contractions per ten minutes as requiring attention.

rules.name: Maternal tachycardia
rules.message: Maternal pulse above 120 — find the cause.
rules.explanation: A maternal pulse above 120 in labour is an LCG alert and points to pain, dehydration, fever, bleeding or sepsis — a rising pulse is often the first sign of concealed haemorrhage or infection.
rules.requiredAction: Look for a cause — bleeding, fever, dehydration, pain — measure blood pressure and temperature, and treat what you find.
sourceRefs: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) — maternal pulse

adaptation.whoStatement: The Labour Care Guide flags a maternal pulse above 120 beats per minute as requiring attention.
evidenceRefs: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) — maternal pulse

rules.name: Raised maternal blood pressure in labour
rules.message: Blood pressure raised in labour — assess for pre-eclampsia.
rules.explanation: A blood pressure of 140/90 or above in labour is an LCG alert; intrapartum hypertension can be the first presentation of pre-eclampsia and needs the same assessment.
rules.requiredAction: Check proteinuria and symptoms of severe pre-eclampsia, and manage per the hypertensive-disorders pathway. A severe reading (160/110) is an emergency.
sourceRefs: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) — blood pressure

adaptation.whoStatement: The Labour Care Guide flags a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or above as requiring attention.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published; management follows the national hypertensive-disorders pathway.
evidenceRefs: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) — blood pressure

rules.name: Maternal temperature outside the reference range
rules.message: Maternal temperature outside 35.5–37.5 — find the cause.
rules.explanation: A temperature of 37.5 or above in labour is an LCG alert for intrapartum infection (including chorioamnionitis), and a low temperature can accompany sepsis or exposure.
rules.requiredAction: Assess for infection — prolonged rupture of membranes, offensive liquor, fetal tachycardia — and treat. Fever in labour is a fetal concern as well as a maternal one.

adaptation.whoStatement: The Labour Care Guide flags a temperature of 37.5 °C or above as requiring attention.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published, with a low-temperature bound added for completeness.
